Moroccan · Easy · Serves 4–6

Loubia is the week's quiet backbone: white beans simmered with a little cured or fresh meat until the pot turns creamy and the broth runs thick with the beans' own starch, ladled over bread or into bowls with cumin and olive oil at the table. Every Mediterranean shore keeps a version — this is the Maghreb's, run with paprika's warmth and the slow pot's patience, the dish that feeds the household on the days when the tagine rests.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • or honestly omitted for the vegetarian week
- **Soak the beans fully and salt them early.** The 8 hours' soak drinks, and a pinch of the salt added to the soaking water (the modern bean law) seasons the bean's interior — the creaminess begins in the soak. The broth's thickness comes from the beans' own starch, and only from it — no flour, no blending: the slow pot's reduction is the loubia's own thickening. - **The bridge:** the kaddid (#52's dried beef) is the traditional flavor-anchor and a specialty — the fresh meat or the honest omission all run true. Everything else is the daily row.

Loubia White Bean Stew

Prep: 20 minutes, plus 8 hours soaking · Cook: 1 hour 30 minutes · Total: About 9 hours 50 minutes (mostly soaking) · Serves 4–6

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 400 g dried white beans (haricot or cannellini), soaked 8 hours
  • 150 g preserved meat (kaddid, the #52's own) or 200 g fresh lamb or beef on the bone, cut small — or honestly omitted for the vegetarian week
  • 1 onion (about 150 g), sliced; 4 cloves garlic (about 15 g), sliced
  • 1 tbsp tomato paste (about 15 g) or 2 grated tomatoes; 1½ tsp paprika; 1 tsp cumin; ½ tsp chile flakes or 1 tsp harissa (#91)
  • 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g); 1½ tsp salt; a fist of cilantro and parsley (about 25 g), tied
  • 1.5 litres water (about 1.5 kg); a carrot (about 100 g), thick-coined, optional
  • To serve: ground cumin and olive oil at the table, lemon wedges, bread (about 300 g), the #104 pickled turnips beside

Instructions

  1. **The base (10 minutes).** Warm the oil in the heavy pot; add the meat (if running), the onion, and the garlic, frying gently 5 minutes to soften. The tomato paste, paprika, cumin, and chile stirred through 1 minute to the pot's perfume. Checkpoint — the paste should darken on the pot's bottom — its raw edge cooking out — and the fragrance runs warm, not sharp. This small fried base is the whole pot's seasoning.
  2. **The long simmer (1 hour 20 minutes).** The drained beans, the water, the herb bundle, and the salt (minus a pinch held for the end) — bring to a bare simmer, cover ajar, and cook at the gentlest bubble 1 hour 10 minutes, until the beans are fully tender and beginning to burst their skins, the broth thickening visibly. The carrot in the last 30 minutes if running. In the final 10 minutes, crush a spoonful of the beans against the pot's side and stir them back — the cream's quick thickening. Checkpoint — the broth's end: creamy-faint, coating the spoon in a film — a stew's broth, not a soup's. The beans should be at the tender-bursting edge, half-whole, half-crumbling into the body. The taste: savory-warm, the paprika's register forward, one notch under final salt.
  3. **The service — the table's own dials.** Ladled deep into bowls or over the torn bread; the ground cumin and the olive oil at each hand, the lemon's wedge, the pickles beside. Checkpoint — eating test: the beans' cream and the broth's body — the meat's savor or the vegetarian's honest depth beneath — a hard shake of cumin over the bowl, the raw olive oil's green poured in a thread, the lemon at the swallow, and the bread sopping the last. It should taste like the week's own food: complete, unfussy, and better the second day when the pot has thickened overnight into the canon's finest leftover.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Broth thin, soupyBeans under-simmered or water over-runThe bursting edge; the last-10-minute crush
Beans tough at the clock's endOld beans or under-soakedThe full 8 hours; more time, not more heat
Pot flat despite the baseMeat or herbs shyThe anchoring choice matters; both broths build

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Keeps 4 days refrigerated, thickening daily (the bean pot's own law); the reheat wants a splash of water. Freezes 2 months. The #88 loubia b'dersa is the fierce Algerian sibling. - Variations: the vegetarian's smoked-paprika depth, the kaddid festival version. The #52 kaddid is the preserved meat's own record on this site.
